title: Tech & architecture slides for the Sanoma deck
subtitle: Two slides: they replace the solution slide and the human-oversight slide, not added on top
footer: Recordly | Sanoma | Analytics backlog agent pilot

slides.title: The agent drafts in a sandbox; only your engineer can merge
bullets: **Your stack, named after day 1.** The RFP says only "public cloud". If your warehouse is Snowflake with dbt, our running agent pattern deploys as is; otherwise the hackathon shows whether it ports, and you can stop.
**Merge requests in your own tool.** Branch protection and required approval by your engineers: the agent has no merge right and no production credentials. Any engineer can pause it.
**Not a black box.** Conventions, examples, prompts and the test set live in your repository; your engineers change the rules without us.

columns.title: Your backlog
boxes: Routine ticket (2-3 classes agreed at the hackathon)
Unclear ticket: questions back on the ticket

columns.title: Agent in a dev sandbox
boxes: Reads ticket, code and model metadata
Writes change and tests on non-prod or masked data

columns.title: Checks
boxes: Review agent: SQL and your conventions
Your CI tests + edge-case regression set
Retry cap, then stops and writes what it tried

columns.title: Your engineer
boxes: Only a person merges to main

diagram.band: In your repository and cloud tenant: branch protection, no agent merge right, no production credentials, run log and cost cap per ticket, pause switch. Model runs in your cloud tenant on your credits; tickets and code leave it nowhere. Retry cap 3 attempts per ticket; cost cap per ticket proposed on day 2 from the hackathon runs

slides.title: Technical gates: you decide at each one, on numbers from your own tickets
table: Repository and merge-request access, a dev schema, 5-8 sample tickets; masking rules agreed if ticket or data samples hold personal data

Feasibility note: stack fit, routine share of the sample, edge cases found, access gaps, baseline lead time. Sanoma decides. Port check on day 1 (<= 2 h): repo and CI access, a dev schema, a model change built and tested by hand. If any fails we say so and the plan stops there
Agent scored on 30-50 of your closed tickets, incl. the ones that "always go wrong"; pass share agreed with you after the first run, not before
Approved without rework, rejected and why, wrong passes, review minutes, lead time vs baseline. Any prompt, model or convention change replays the test set first
slides.note: Technical unknowns, resolved on day 1: warehouse and transformation tool; Git and ticket host; share of the backlog that is routine; personal data in subscriber analytics. If the answer is "little routine work", we say so at the gate.
